correctness.rationale: Strict convexity and superlinearity on x>=0 give unique minimizer; derivative -infinity at x_i=0 forces interior. KKT yields positive monotone scalar root F(t)=b+λt with x_i=c_i exp(-a_i t). As bλ→0, t→infinity, with λt<=Me^(-alpha t) implying t=O(log1/λ). For finite b/(λL)→β, lower bound F>=Ce^(-alpha t) gives t/L→1/alpha and F(t)~(β+1/alpha)λL. For dominant b≫λL, λt=o(b), hence F(t)~b. At b=0, z=alpha t and w=W(alpha C/λ), use 0<=z-w<=log(1+R(z/alpha)) with R=O(e^-δz); the stated relative Lambert correction follows. Shape convergence and non-Lipschitz at λ0 are direct. Independent fresh 70-digit KKT bisections covered heterogeneous, tied minima, zero, finite-ratio and data-dominated regimes; all residuals <1e-65 and zero-data relative errors tiny at λ=1e-24; finite β transient relative ~0.056 is consistent with slow log convergence. Numerical checks are diagnostic only.

value.rationale: The exact transition scale λlog(1/λ), minimum-forward-coefficient support selection, coordinate-specific powers a_i/alpha, and singular non-Lipschitz endpoint quantify a mathematically meaningful inverse-problem boundary where standard fixed-mass stability is inapplicable. Though scalarizable, this is a complete natural phase classification, not a routine KKT restatement.
